request: We'd like managers to edit and re-approve documents after they've already been signed.

problem.evidence: Request states the desired action (edit + re-approve post-signature) but not the driver — error correction? periodic policy update? a compliance mandate? This changes whether it's a rare exception path or a routine workflow.

current_process.evidence: Unknown whether managers already work around this today (e.g. re-uploading as a new document manually) or whether this is entirely unsupported today.

success_metrics.evidence: No stated measure of success (faster correction cycle? fewer off-system edits? audit pass rate?).

actors.evidence: Managers are named explicitly as the ones editing and re-approving. Unclear whether original signatories, compliance/records officers, or other circuit reviewers are still involved.

business_objects.evidence: Per the Document/Version model, 'editing a signed document' almost always means creating a new Version while the prior signed one is retained — the request doesn't say whether this matches the client's intent or whether they picture an in-place change.

business_rules.evidence: Unclear whether the re-approval circuit after an edit must mirror the original signature circuit (same signatories) or whether manager sign-off alone suffices — a materially different build and a different legal posture.

workflow.evidence: The approval/signature lifecycle and the publication/distribution lifecycle are independent in this product. The request only addresses re-approval; it's silent on whether the re-approved version automatically becomes the published/current one.

integrations.evidence: Who gets notified when a signed document is edited and re-approved (readers of the old version, downstream systems referencing it) is unaddressed.

permissions.evidence: Unclear whether any manager can edit any signed document, or whether this is gated by classification level (confidential/restricted) or by document ownership.

config_vs_custom.evidence: Whether this edit-and-reapprove capability is a global platform rule or configurable per client (approval circuits and classification schemes already vary by client) is unaddressed.

constraints.evidence: Regulatory/electronic-signature validity is directly at stake: editing a signed document normally invalidates prior signatures and requires re-collection — unaddressed, and named as a sensitivity in the product context.

edge_cases.evidence: What if the document is under legal hold, mid-retention, or has a pending prior re-approval when a second edit arrives? Not covered.

reporting.evidence: An audit trail is a standard, non-negotiable feature of the platform; re-approval after signature is exactly the kind of event (who edited, when, previous vs new content, who re-approved) that trail must capture without gaps — raised to high given the regulatory sensitivity named in the context.

risks.evidence: Main risk: silently invalidating legally-relied-upon signatures, or confusing 'approved' with 'published/current' at rollout.

challenges.headline: Manager-only re-approval
challenges.premise: The request implies the manager who edits the document can also re-approve it alone.
challenges.alternative: Route the new version back through the same signature circuit as the original — or use a materiality tier, where minor edits need manager sign-off and substantive edits need the full circuit.
challenges.consequence: Manager-only re-approval may not carry the same legal weight as the original signature, leaving the status of prior relied-upon signatures ambiguous.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm with legal/compliance whether original signatories must re-sign, and under what threshold a lighter review is acceptable.

challenges.headline: Approval auto-becomes publication
challenges.premise: The request treats 're-approve' as if it immediately makes the edited document the live one everyone sees.
challenges.alternative: Keep publication a distinct, manager-triggered step after re-approval, as the platform already separates the approval/signature lifecycle from publication/distribution.
challenges.consequence: Auto-publishing on re-approval could release a freshly-changed document to readers the moment a manager signs, skipping any intended review-before-release window.
challenges.recommendation: Decide explicitly, before build, whether re-approval auto-publishes or requires a separate publish action.

challenges.headline: Ungated edit trigger
challenges.premise: The request names managers broadly as the ones who can edit and re-approve, without scoping by classification or document ownership.
challenges.alternative: Gate the edit-trigger capability by the document's classification level and/or ownership, consistent with how read/visibility access already works on this platform.
challenges.consequence: An ungated capability lets any manager reopen any signed document — including confidential or restricted ones outside their remit — a wide blast radius given how cross-cutting classification already is.
challenges.recommendation: Define the permission gate (classification and/or ownership) before implementation, not at acceptance testing.

decisions.tradeoff: More version-history data and reconciliation work carried forward, in exchange for keeping the audit trail and signature validity intact.

decisions.decision: Edits to a signed document will follow the platform's standard supersession pattern — a new version, the signed one retained and referenceable — not an in-place modification.
decisions.why: In-place editing of a signed version is excluded by the platform's core frozen-after-approval rule, which is standard for every client.
decisions.tradeoff: More build complexity (versioning, re-approval, signature handling) in exchange for keeping the signature and audit trail legally defensible.

decisions.decision: The prior signed version is retained and stays referenceable after supersession.

exclusions.option: Generalizing the supersession/re-approval flow across all document types in this same phase
exclusions.reason: The named regulatory constraints (e-signature validity, retention) must be satisfied correctly for the core edit path first; extending to every document type in parallel multiplies compliance exposure before the pattern is proven.

thresholds.condition: Re-approval is confirmed to require a legally binding e-signature event, not just an internal sign-off
thresholds.measure: whether the regulatory e-signature validity requirement applies to the re-approval step
thresholds.action: integrate a certified e-signature re-signing step instead of a simple approval stamp

thresholds.condition: The document being edited is classified restricted or confidential
thresholds.measure: the document's classification level at edit time
thresholds.action: route the edit through an additional compliance/records-officer review rather than manager-only approval
